lead.headline: U.S. widens strikes on Iran; Tehran answers at bases in three countries
lead.dek: Iran says one strike hit a wedding near the Strait of Hormuz, killing at least 5; Jordan intercepted 10 missiles.
body: The U.S. military struck Iranian air-defense sites, radar, maritime assets and communications facilities Tuesday, and Iran answered overnight with ballistic missiles and drones aimed at U.S. bases in Jordan, Bahrain and Kuwait. Jordan's military said it intercepted 10 missiles, with three falling in unpopulated areas; Kuwait and Bahrain reported downing drones.

Central Command said the strikes followed attempted Revolutionary Guard attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, where two tankers were hit Monday. Iranian officials said one strike hit a home hosting a wedding in coastal Kuhestak, killing at least five people and wounding more than 60; Al Jazeera verified the location, and Central Command said it was aware of the reports.

Trump warned that Iran "will be hit again at a much harder and higher level" if it retaliates, while President Masoud Pezeshkian offered a return to the June ceasefire if Washington reciprocates. The Revolutionary Guard claimed it targeted a U.S. base near Aqaba; the U.S. said no bases were hit, and a parliament official said the strikes "will not go unpunished."

briefs.headline: House passes stopgap funding the government through Dec. 11
briefs.summary: The 370-48 vote sends the measure to Trump; it bars homeland security fund transfers to the Border Patrol and delays a rule letting political appointees halt federal grants.

briefs.headline: Whistleblower calls new USPS mail-ballot system untested
briefs.summary: A disclosure released by Sen. Blumenthal says the portal was built in three months and rejects a whole ballot batch over one bad barcode; Judge Talwani hears the injunction bid Thursday.

briefs.headline: Oil climbs out of its summer range as Hormuz traffic thins
briefs.summary: Brent rose about 2% Tuesday to $92.31 a barrel; strait transits fell to 107 last week from 121, against a prewar norm near 130 a day, with many tankers sailing with transponders off.

briefs.headline: Edouard comes ashore at Johnson Bayou, soaks Texas as it fades
briefs.summary: The season's fifth Atlantic storm made landfall Tuesday with 60 mph winds and weakened to a depression by night; 3 to 6 inches of rain, locally 9, threaten flash flooding through today.

briefs.headline: Nepal's flood toll reaches 1,114 with 3,916 still missing
briefs.summary: The disaster authority said Wednesday that 11,993 people have been rescued since the Aug. 26 Bhotekoshi flood, with more than 21,300 security personnel deployed across eight districts.

briefs.headline: Germany blames Russia for Leipzig airport drone, shuts consulate
briefs.summary: Interior Minister Dobrindt said the August explosive drone "fits the known pattern of Russian hybrid operations"; the Bonn consulate closes by Sept. 18, and Moscow called the charge absurd.

briefs.headline: Hichilema sworn in for a second term with his rival jailed
briefs.summary: Zambia's president took the oath Tuesday after a 60%-38% win over Brian Mundubile, who faces treason charges along with about a dozen opposition figures; courts closed as legal challenges loomed, Human Rights Watch said.

briefs.headline: Israeli strikes kill at least 5 in Gaza despite the ceasefire
briefs.summary: Hospital sources said a drone strike west of Gaza City killed three people, two of them children; Defense Minister Katz said the strikes covered an arrest operation that "was discovered."

briefs.headline: Treasurer projects $100M a year in taxes from two data centers
briefs.summary: The office's analysis of the $10B Penzance project in Berkeley County and Google's $7B Putnam County build projects $8.3M a year for Putnam's commission and $17.4M for its schools, plus $27.9M for the income-tax reduction fund.

briefs.headline: Ridgeline permit opponents head to the state Supreme Court
briefs.summary: Tucker United, the Highlands Conservancy, the Sierra Club and Appalachian Mountain Advocates say they will refile their challenge to the data-center campus's air permit after the Intermediate Court dismissed it on jurisdiction.

briefs.headline: Chamber opens its 90th Business Summit at The Greenbrier
briefs.summary: The three-day annual meeting runs today through Friday under the theme "A Legacy That Leads," the chamber's 90th such gathering.

regional.item: Huntington ran the first of three floodwall gate exercises Tuesday at Altizer Avenue; Guyandotte's Main Street gate follows Sept. 10.
A Kanawha County grand jury returned dozens of indictments this week, including child-abuse, robbery and bomb-threat cases.
Crews broke ground Tuesday on the Rend Trail rehabilitation in the New River Gorge park - five trestles, retaining walls and the Minden trailhead.

away.item: The Vermont Veterans Home hosts Bennington's 25th-anniversary Sept. 11 ceremony at its Memorial Wall, with wreaths and a 21-gun salute.

hotspots.item: The Webster County Fair, billed as the state's oldest, runs Sept. 9-12 at Camp Caesar with live music and 4-H exhibits daily.
Surf City put out an Aug. 31 call for a real-estate appraiser for its federal beach nourishment project; proposals are due Oct. 2.

briefs.headline: Treed island the size of a football field drifts across Williston
briefs.summary: BC Hydro confirmed by satellite that the treed mat, about 140 by 70 meters, drifted 30 km before vanishing from view; it likely broke loose when the reservoir filled fully for the first time in 14 years.

briefs.headline: Findlay stakes her leadership on the Abbotsford-Mission vote
briefs.summary: With seven MLAs gone from the B.C. Conservative caucus since early August, the leader says she is putting her full energy into the Sept. 26 byelection; one analyst called it "a party imploding before our eyes."

briefs.headline: Carney says U.S. terms would see Canadian industries 'wiped out'
briefs.summary: The prime minister said Washington wants core industries, autos included, made subsidiaries of American firms - terms he rejected - as Canada's counter-tariffs on 700 U.S. products take effect Monday.

briefs.headline: Roman telescope opens its antenna and visor, powers up imager
briefs.summary: The high-gain antenna and sunshade deployed within a day of each other after Sunday's launch; the coronagraph powered on Tuesday for months of calibration, with first images expected in early 2027.

briefs.headline: Snake embryos all coil right, and a gut 'pillar' explains why
briefs.summary: CT scans of more than 900 embryos across 39 species show the body outgrowing the gut, which tethers to yolk vessels on the left and buckles the lengthening body rightward, researchers report in Current Biology.

briefs.headline: Hunting one exotic particle, GlueX turns up two others
briefs.summary: The Jefferson Lab collaboration reports structures at 2.24 GeV with 5-sigma significance and 1.82 GeV at 3 sigma in Physical Review Letters - possible exotic arrangements of strange quarks and excited gluons.

briefs.headline: Oxidizer leak grounds Crew-13 with no new launch date set
briefs.summary: NASA and SpaceX stood down Friday from the Sept. 12 target after the leak turned up in the Dragon capsule's propulsion system; the four-member crew is bound for a seven-month station stay.

briefs.headline: EU opens first AI Act enforcement as U.S. pushes the other way
briefs.summary: The AI Office sent information requests to more than 30 model providers Tuesday covering security, evaluations and training-content disclosures, while U.S. officials pitched deregulatory "Carolina Principles" at a G20 ministerial.

briefs.headline: FSB chief calls frontier AI the top cyber risk to finance
briefs.summary: In an Aug. 31 letter to G20 finance ministers, Andrew Bailey said models show "increasingly sophisticated autonomy" and "threat capabilities" that could change the speed and economics of cyber risk.
